clue.text: One has a record or disc with loud guitar

parts.note: a disc is round, like the letter O
F is forte, the musical direction for loud
Fender is a famous make of electric guitar

explanation.surface: A musician owns a record or a disc, plus a loud electric guitar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record' tempts as a music term beside disc and guitar; here it is a criminal record.
explanation.definitionFit: An offender is someone with a criminal record, someone convicted of a crime.

clue.text: Single person who may be duped immediately

parts.note: a single one is A
a sap is a gullible fool, easily taken in

explanation.surface: A lone gullible person is fooled straight away.
explanation.definitionFit: ASAP abbreviates 'as soon as possible', meaning at once.

clue.text: Old fellows ignored remnant of material

parts.note: F is fellow, so FF is the plural
to cut someone is to snub or ignore them

explanation.surface: Elderly members of a club pay no attention to a scrap of cloth.
explanation.definitionFit: An offcut is a leftover piece trimmed from fabric, wood or similar stock.

clue.text: Government department uncovered waste product

indicators.note: with its covering stripped off, the word loses its outer letters at both ends

parts.note: a bureau is an office or department of government

explanation.surface: A ministry is exposed for producing rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Uncovered' removes the first and last letters, B and U, from BUREAU.
explanation.definitionFit: Urea is the nitrogen compound the body excretes in urine.

clue.text: Spat with Victor on street in Great Depression

parts.note: a spat is a quarrel, a rift
Victor is V in the NATO phonetic alphabet
an alley is a narrow street

explanation.surface: A quarrel with someone called Victor out on the road during the 1930s slump.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great Depression' looks like the economic slump; it points to the Great Rift Valley of East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: A rift valley is a sunken trough in the earth's crust; the Great Rift Valley is the best-known.

clue.text: One wears silver kind of skirt on number of fields

indicators.note: in a down clue, the letters placed on the number come above it

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: something worn is held inside, so the one sits within the other letters

parts.note: a rara skirt is a short ruffled skirt
one is I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: Someone in a silver ruffled skirt stands on a figure in the fields.
explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside AGRARA to make AGRARIA, then N follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Agrarian is an adjective for anything relating to farmland and its cultivation.

clue.text: Then is no one getting charged in affray?

definitions.text: Then is no one getting charged
definitions.meaning: if no one pays a charge, entry is free for everybody
an affray is a brawl, a fight where everyone joins in

explanation.walkthrough: 'Charged' looks like a criminal charge after a brawl; the first reading means charged a fee.
explanation.definitionFit: A free-for-all is a disorderly fight in which anyone may join, as in a public brawl.

clue.text: Current unit in van wanting leader on base

indicators.note: in a down clue, the first part sits on top of the second
lacking its leader means the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a camper is a camper van
e is the base of natural logarithms

explanation.surface: An electrical part is stowed in a vehicle, short of a driver back at base.
explanation.walkthrough: CAMPER loses its first letter to give AMPER.
explanation.definitionFit: The ampere is the SI unit of electric current.

clue.text: Raffish rogue, cool entering car, shows breeding

indicators.note: rogue as an adjective means wayward, out of control, so the letters stray into a new order
the one goes into the other

parts.note: MG is a classic British make of car
in means fashionable, cool

explanation.surface: A disreputable rascal, slick as he slides into his car, displays good upbringing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' reads as a noun beside 'Raffish', but it is an adjective-style anagram signal turning RAFFISH into FISHFAR. 'Breeding' looks like good manners; here it is raising fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Fish farming is the raising of fish in tanks or pens, a form of breeding stock.

clue.text: Jollies around India's border

indicators.note: the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: Jollies is nickname slang for the Royal Marines, RM
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Fun outings round the edge of India.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jollies' looks like fun trips; it is the old naval nickname for Royal Marines.
explanation.definitionFit: A rim is the edge or margin of something.

clue.text: Surviving without sports clubs, or in the club

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the first word surrounds the others

parts.note: extant means still in existence, surviving
PE is physical education, school sports
C is the card-suit abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Someone getting by with no sporting clubs to belong to, or else belonging to one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' means outside, not lacking. 'In the club' is British slang for pregnant.
explanation.definitionFit: Expectant means pregnant, which the slang phrase 'in the club' also means.

clue.text: Pop diva has drink, drinking case of Drambuie

indicators.note: drinking takes something in, so the one encloses the other

parts.note: ale is beer, a drink

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A pop star has a beer while downing a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case of' takes D and E from Drambuie, which go inside ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Adele is a British singer, one of the best-selling female pop stars.

clue.text: Democrat given punishment, about to resign

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: time is slang for a prison sentence

explanation.surface: A Democratic politician, having been sentenced, is on the point of quitting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'About' turns TIME into EMIT.
explanation.definitionFit: To demit is a formal word for giving up an office, to step down.

clue.text: Heading for match, cool guy is excitedly studying the scores

indicators.note: the heading of a word is its first letter
excited letters jump about into a new order

explanation.surface: At the start of the game, a laid-back chap gets worked up checking the results.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Excitedly' rearranges COOLGUYIS to USICOLOGY. 'Scores' looks like match results; it means musical scores.
explanation.definitionFit: Musicology is the academic study of music, including written scores.

clue.text: Woe is me, sadly: hosting a Republican's tedious

indicators.note: a host takes guests in, so the rearranged letters enclose the rest
sadly suggests things going wrong, so the letters fall into a different order

explanation.surface: A lament about entertaining a Republican, who proves boring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sadly' rearranges WOEISME, and AR goes inside to make WEARISOME.
explanation.definitionFit: Wearisome means tiresome and dull, causing fatigue or boredom.

clue.text: Mythical female means to catch bird with speed

indicators.note: catching holds something within, so one word encloses the other

parts.note: a way is a means or method
a tern is a seabird
mph, miles per hour, is a measure of speed

explanation.surface: A legendary woman plans to snare a bird quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: A water nymph is a spirit of rivers or springs in Greek legend, such as a naiad.

clue.text: Singing flier forgetting day for launch again

indicators.note: forgetting leaves something out

parts.note: the redstart is a songbird

explanation.surface: A songbird loses track of the date before setting off once more.
explanation.walkthrough: REDSTART drops its D.
explanation.definitionFit: To restart is to begin or set something going a second time.

clue.text: Nothing left is fine

definitions.meaning: if nothing is on the left, everything is on the right side

explanation.walkthrough: 'Left' looks like remaining; read it as the opposite of right.
explanation.definitionFit: All right is everyday speech for acceptable or okay.

clue.text: Piece of dialogue, bar changes, in script

parts.note: a line is one spoken piece in a play

indicators.note: changes signals the letters swapping places

explanation.surface: An actor's speech in a play, with musical bars altered, appears in the screenplay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Changes' rearranges BAR to ARB.
explanation.definitionFit: Linear B is an ancient writing system used for Mycenaean Greek.

clue.text: Most flamboyant cream clothing foolhardy?

indicators.note: clothing covers, so one word wraps around the other

parts.note: the cream is the best of something
rash means reckless, foolhardy

explanation.surface: Is wearing the cream outfit reckless?
explanation.definitionFit: Brash means loud and showy, so the brashest is the showiest of all.

clue.text: Not seriously concerned with viewer getting covered in jelly, oddly

indicators.note: covered in means wrapped around, so the second piece sits inside the first
oddly takes the odd-numbered letters of the word

parts.note: ocular means relating to the eye, the viewer

explanation.surface: Joking about an eye that ends up smeared in jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Oddly' gives J, L, Y from jelly; OCULAR goes inside after the J.
explanation.definitionFit: Jocularly means in a joking, light-hearted manner.

clue.text: Rabbit punch lands on British head of state

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece lands on top of the rest

parts.note: a jab is a short quick punch
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch, Britain's head of state

explanation.surface: A rabbit punch connects with a British monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like part of the phrase 'rabbit punch'; it is the definition, British slang for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (on) is British slang for talking at length, as is to jabber.

clue.text: President Arthur's beginning to take steps

parts.note: James K. Polk was the 11th US president

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: President Chester Arthur's first move is to take action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'President Arthur' suggests Chester A. Arthur, but the president is Polk. 'Take steps' looks like acting; it means dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To polka is to dance the lively Bohemian polka, stepping in time.

clue.text: What may beat the blues for Baron Goldsmith

parts.note: pro means in favour of, for
Zac Goldsmith, a British politician, was made Baron Goldsmith

explanation.surface: A financier's remedy for gloom.
explanation.definitionFit: Prozac is a brand of antidepressant, a cure for feeling low.

clue.text: Hot food is very cold, but not cold

indicators.note: but not signals a letter to be dropped

parts.note: Baltic is British slang for freezing weather
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A spicy dish served freezing, though not cold: a contradiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Baltic' is British slang for bitterly cold, from the Baltic Sea; it loses its C.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spicy curry cooked and served in a metal bowl.

clue.text: Maybe Amber is to cry with love and longing

parts.note: to yell is to cry out
love means zero in tennis, the letter O
a wish is a longing or desire

explanation.surface: A woman named Amber wants to weep with affection and yearning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Amber' looks like a woman's name; it is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Amber is a golden orange colour, a shade near yellow, so an example of yellowish.

clue.text: John Travolta's first to get sack

parts.note: john is slang for a toilet, a loo

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter

explanation.surface: The actor John Travolta is the first to be fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'John' looks like the actor's first name; it is a toilet. 'Sack' is a verb, to plunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To loot is to plunder or pillage, as an army sacks a town.

clue.text: Slender and delicate wife leaves game

indicators.note: leaving means going away, so the letter is dropped

parts.note: wispy means thin and fine, like a wisp

explanation.surface: A frail, thin wife walks out on the match.
explanation.definitionFit: I spy is a children's guessing game based on initial letters.

clue.text: Some work thus finishes early

indicators.note: stopping before the end means the last letter is cut

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore, thus

explanation.surface: Part of the job is done, so it wraps up ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: An erg is a unit of work or energy in the CGS system.

clue.text: A bit of brains in joint work around university

parts.note: the hip is a joint

indicators.note: around means turned round, so it is read backwards

parts.note: op is short for opus, a work
a campus is a university's grounds, standing for the university

explanation.surface: A clever piece of joint research at a college.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' makes PO; 'joint work' looks like a collaboration but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: The hippocampus is a region of the brain involved in memory.
